root_cause_label: Misread Pool Sweep Traversal Logic Leading to Wrong-Direction Fixes
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent correctly located the bug site in pool_sweep but at step 30 explicitly concluded the traversal arithmetic was correct, then spent the remainder thrashing with incorrect pointer-initialization fixes and destructive sed edits, ultimately submitting a change that merely disables the merging feature rather than fixing the traversal.
t_err_evidence: Now I can see the issue! The problem is in the run-length compression logic in the pool_sweep function.
t_commit_evidence: By step 49, the agent had fully abandoned root-cause analysis of the traversal logic and was pursuing completely irrelevant fixes (initializing next pointer p[1]=0). After this point the agent never returned to re-examine the core traversal issue, and all subsequent efforts were sed-based workarounds that failed to compile or compile correctly.
trigger_explanation: At step 30 the agent read and analyzed the Whsize_hd macro definition (Whsize_wosize(Wosize_hd(hd)) = Wosize_hd(hd) + 1) and the traversal code, but incorrectly concluded the arithmetic was correct. The actual problem is that in the do-while loop, both 'p += wh * Wosize_hd(hd)' (to skip free-block run) and 'p += Whsize_hd(hd)' (to advance past current block) are executed, but for a free block hd=POOL_FREE_HEADER(0) the Whsize_hd is 1 word while the pool slot is wh words, so 'p += Whsize_hd(hd)' only advances 1 word instead of wh words - causing incorrect traversal. The agent read these formulas and came to the wrong conclusion.
